$comment: A corpus of diary situations, each written to probe one way the Insights view could mislead.
Every scenario is deterministic: the feelings are the ones a user settled on, and the topics
come from the keyword extractor, so no model runs and the right answer can be worked out by
hand. `expect` always describes what the app SHOULD do, never what it currently does.
holds  - the app already meets the expectation, and the test guards it.
defect - it does not. The test is run as a failing expectation, so fixing the underlying
problem turns the suite red and forces this file to be updated alongside it.
Sources are per scenario: the repo's own research under specs/research, the self-tracking
literature on confounding and reverse causation, or plain reasoning about the code.

scenarios.name: walking lifts energy
scenarios.concern: The happy path. A real habit, written plainly, three times over.

entries.text: Went for a walk at lunch instead of eating at my desk.
Walked home the long way and felt awake again.
Short walk around the block between meetings.
Stayed in all evening, nothing much happened.
Quiet day indoors, routine chores only.
Another quiet day indoors, routine chores only.
A third quiet day indoors, routine chores only.
A fourth quiet day indoors, routine chores only.
A fifth quiet day indoors, routine chores only.

scenarios.note: P0-6: the diary needs at least one day off from walking to compare against, or the lift is a division by zero and the badge this scenario is about would not show at all — 'A real habit' has to mean a real ratio, not just three good days with nothing to weigh them against.

scenarios.name: two occurrences stay quiet
scenarios.concern: Two is a coincidence. The threshold is the only defence against reading meaning into noise.

entries.text: Pizza for dinner again.
Pizza again, second night running.

scenarios.name: an entry that is only a feeling
scenarios.concern: No topic at all. There is nothing to correlate, and the app must not invent one.

entries.text: Flat.
Low again.
Not great.

scenarios.name: a word inside another word
scenarios.concern: Topic extraction on word boundaries, which a previous implementation got wrong.

entries.text: The network was down and I had homework to finish.
Network problems again, plus homework.
More network trouble. Homework still not done.
Waited a long time at the shop for nothing.
Sat quietly for a while, nothing else happening.
Another quiet spell, nothing else happening.
A third quiet spell, nothing else happening.
A fourth quiet spell, nothing else happening.

scenarios.note: 'network' must not register as 'work'. 'homework' correctly registers as 'study'. P0-6: the shop/quiet-spell entries give the pattern a real comparison group — without one the lift is a division by zero and 'direction' would read 'none' regardless of the extraction question this scenario is actually about.

scenarios.name: a long run of the same habit
scenarios.concern: Counts scale without the sentence becoming absurd.

entries.text: A slow start to the day, feeling low.
Another slow start, feeling low.
Nothing much today, felt oddly fine.

scenarios.note: P0-6: the three added entries give the pattern a real comparison group (one walk-free day still felt energised, two did not) — 20 identical entries and nothing to weigh them against is a division by zero, not a lift, and would leave the pattern's badge withheld regardless of the count itself.

scenarios.name: a habit the writer explicitly did not have
scenarios.concern: Negation. The entry says the topic did NOT happen, and the extractor counts it anyway.

entries.text: No coffee at all today, and I slept properly for once.
Skipped the coffee again. Another decent night.
Still no coffee. Sleeping much better without it.

scenarios.note: The true reading is the opposite of what is recorded: coffee's ABSENCE is what goes with feeling calm.

scenarios.name: an intention, not an event
scenarios.concern: Hypothetical and future-tense mentions are counted as things that happened.

entries.text: I should really cut down on the wine one of these days.
Keep telling myself I will give up wine in the new year.
Thinking again about quitting wine for a while.

scenarios.note: Nobody drank anything. The insight reads as though they did.

scenarios.name: somebody else's habit
scenarios.concern: A topic belonging to another person is attributed to the writer.

entries.text: My colleague drank another coffee before the meeting. I had water.
Colleague on the coffee again all morning. Water for me.
Watched my colleague finish a coffee in one go. I stuck to water.

scenarios.note: The writer drank water every time. The insight will be about coffee they never had.

scenarios.name: a dominant mood makes everything look causal
scenarios.concern: Base rate. When one feeling fills the diary, every topic co-occurs with it and every co-occurrence crosses the threshold.

entries.text: Long day at work.
Work again, back to back.
Another day of work.
Walked to the shops.
Walked into town.
Walked the dog, twice.
Had tea in the garden.
Tea with my sister.
Made a pot of tea and read.

scenarios.note: Fixed by A3. Every topic here co-occurs with exhaustion at exactly the base rate, so lift is 1.0x for all three and all three are suppressed. The >=3 rule still passes them; lift is what tells them apart from a real finding.

scenarios.name: two things that always happen together
scenarios.concern: Confounding. Coffee and bad sleep never appear apart, so each is reported as an independent influence.
scenarios.source: n-of-1 self-tracking literature on unmeasured confounding; addressed by roadmap I2

entries.text: Espresso late again and then barely slept.
Late espresso, slept badly.
Coffee after dinner. Slept terribly.

scenarios.note: Addressed by I2, and deliberately not by hiding either pattern (I2-07). The fixture used to ask for at most one insight; its own note said showing both is defensible if the view says they always co-occur, and that is now exactly what it says.

scenarios.name: the feeling came first
scenarios.concern: Reverse causation. The writer walks BECAUSE they feel low, and the insight reads as though walking makes them low.

entries.text: Felt awful this morning so I made myself go for a walk.
Low again. Went out for a walk to try to shift it.
Rough day, forced myself out for a walk.

scenarios.note: The advice points at reducing walking, which is the coping strategy, not the cause. This is the most actively harmful failure in the set.

scenarios.name: medication
scenarios.concern: Safety. A negative feeling around medication produces advice pointed at changing it.
scenarios.source: reasoning about the curated topic list

entries.text: Started the new medication this week.
Second day on the medication, wiped out.
Medication again this morning. No energy at all.
Exhausted by evening for no particular reason.
Had a good day out, nothing eventful.
Another good day out, nothing eventful.

scenarios.note: The correlation is worth surfacing — it is worth telling a doctor. Advice to change it is not the app's to give. P0-6: the three added entries give the pattern a real comparison group, so the lift is a genuine, threshold-clearing number rather than a division by zero -- this defect must hold on its own numbers, not survive only because the diary was too small to compute one.

scenarios.name: menstrual cycle
scenarios.concern: Safety. A biological cycle is not a behaviour, and 'consider changing it' is not advice.
scenarios.source: reasoning about the curated topic list

entries.text: Got my period today, everything aches.
Second day of my period. Flat.
On my period still. No energy.
Exhausted by evening for no particular reason.
Had a good day out, nothing eventful.
Another good day out, nothing eventful.

scenarios.note: P0-6: the three added entries give the pattern a real comparison group, so the lift is a genuine, threshold-clearing number rather than a division by zero -- this defect must hold on its own numbers, not survive only because the diary was too small to compute one.

scenarios.name: illness
scenarios.concern: Safety. Being ill is not a habit to reduce.
scenarios.source: reasoning about the curated topic list

entries.text: Came down with the flu.
Still sick, stayed in bed.
Third day ill. Wrecked.
Exhausted by evening for no particular reason.
Had a good day out, nothing eventful.
Another good day out, nothing eventful.

scenarios.note: P0-6: the three added entries give the pattern a real comparison group, so the lift is a genuine, threshold-clearing number rather than a division by zero -- this defect must hold on its own numbers, not survive only because the diary was too small to compute one.

scenarios.name: a person, not a habit
scenarios.concern: Tone and safety. A relationship topic pointed at 'change' reads as advice to see less of someone.
scenarios.source: reasoning about the curated topic list

entries.text: Another argument with my partner.
Argued with my partner again this evening.
Disagreement with my partner over nothing.
Felt down for no particular reason this evening.
A pleasant, easy day today.
Another pleasant, easy day today.

scenarios.note: 'conflict' is the useful insight from these entries. 'partner' is the same data pointed at a person. P0-6: the three added entries give the pattern a real comparison group, so the lift is a genuine, threshold-clearing number rather than a division by zero -- this defect must hold on its own numbers, not survive only because the diary was too small to compute one.

scenarios.name: someone in crisis
scenarios.concern: Safety. Entries describing hopelessness and isolation get the same lifestyle-tweak treatment as coffee.

entries.text: Spent the whole weekend alone again. Cannot see the point.
Alone all day. Nothing is going to change.
By myself again. It does not get better.
Felt hopeless for no particular reason today.
A pleasant, easy day with others.
Another pleasant, easy day with others.

scenarios.note: 'Consider reducing time alone' to someone writing this is glib at best. The app has no notion of severity and no crisis path. P0-6: the three added entries give the pattern a real comparison group, so the lift is a genuine, threshold-clearing number rather than a division by zero -- this defect must hold on its own numbers, not survive only because the diary was too small to compute one.

scenarios.name: one entry, four feelings, two topics
scenarios.concern: Multiple comparisons. Every extra feeling multiplies the pairs a single entry contributes.

entries.text: Coffee and a walk before work.
Walk first, then coffee at the desk.
Morning coffee, quick walk.

scenarios.note: Three entries produce eight insights, four of them contradicting the other four, and the view cannot rank them.

scenarios.name: the same topic pointing both ways
scenarios.concern: Contradiction. Two insights about one topic, one saying keep and one saying change.

entries.text: Morning coffee, felt great.
Coffee with breakfast, good start.
Coffee before the walk, lovely.
Coffee too late, wired all night.
Late coffee again, could not settle.
Evening coffee. Restless.
A good day today, feeling upbeat.
A jittery day, on edge for no reason.
A quiet, uneventful afternoon.
Another quiet, uneventful afternoon.
A third quiet, uneventful afternoon.
A fourth quiet, uneventful afternoon.

scenarios.note: Both are true. The view sets them side by side with nothing to say that the difference is the time of day. P0-6: the six added entries (none mentioning coffee) give both patterns a real comparison group, so each carries a genuine, threshold-clearing lift -- two real, opposite findings about the same topic, not an artefact of a diary too small to compute either ratio.

scenarios.name: the same diary reads the same way twice
scenarios.concern: Stability. Re-reading Insights must not reshuffle the list under the reader.

entries.text: Tea in the evening.
Tea before bed.
Pot of tea, quiet night.

scenarios.note: Ordering is by last_updated_at with the pattern id as tiebreaker, so a diary reads consistently. What it is NOT ordered by is strength: measured over 8 fresh diaries, 7 put a 3-occurrence insight above a 20-occurrence one. That gap is real but arbitrary rather than reliably wrong, so it is recorded in TESTING.md instead of as a test that would flake.

scenarios.name: old entries described as recent
scenarios.concern: Recency. The sentence says 'recent' and the engine has no time window at all.
scenarios.source: reasoning about the narrative wording; fixed by roadmap I3

entries.text: Tea in the garden.
Tea on the balcony.
Pot of tea and a book.

scenarios.note: Fixed by I3. The count is now windowed, so a pattern last seen over a year ago is labelled historical rather than reported as recent — and it is still there, because silently dropping it would be its own defect (I3-09).

scenarios.name: a neutral feeling
scenarios.concern: Neutral has no positive signal, so the direction is 'change' — advice to alter something that was fine.

entries.text: Tea and a quiet evening.
Tea, nothing much happened.
Quiet night in with tea.

scenarios.note: P0-2: a neutral-valence feeling now gets no badge ('none') instead of being folded into 'change'. 'You felt neutral 3 times around tea - consider changing it.' Nothing needs changing.

scenarios.name: written in another language
scenarios.concern: The curated keyword list is English only, so a diary kept in another language yields nothing.
scenarios.source: reasoning about the curated topic list

entries.text: Sétáltam egyet ebédszünetben, sokkal jobb lett a délután.
Megint sétáltam munka után, feltöltődtem.
Rövid séta a ház körül, jólesett.

scenarios.note: Three clear entries about walking produce nothing. The view says 'not enough data yet', which is not what happened.
